problem: Modular GOAT-style methods populate their memory through a fixed-vocabulary detector and 2D semantic maps, so novel open-vocabulary targets are never memorized and 3D spatial-semantic consistency is lost. End-to-end RL methods generalize poorly. Prior 3DGS navigation methods need dense, high-fidelity RGB views.
motivation: Home robots must handle multi-modal (category, image, text), open-vocabulary goals, and many sequential goals in one environment. A memory built once from rapid exploration should serve all later queries. GOAT-Bench is also short and noisy (about 8 subtasks per episode, ambiguous labels), so it is a weak test of long-term memory.
key_idea: Build a codebook-quantized language 3D Gaussian Splatting memory during one-time frontier exploration, query it with CLIP embeddings for candidate waypoints, and confirm targets with on-site perception-based verification.
insight: The 3DGS memory is only a coarse global prior, so verifying on-site is needed because renders from sparse views are blurry. The ablation shows the codebook is critical: replacing it with a 2D-trained autoencoder drops localization from 70.8% to 34.6%. Keyframe retrieval raises PSNR from 21.15 to 27.20 and localization from 66.3% to 70.8%. Verification with LightGlue and SEEM+CLIP raises SR from 41.3% with no verification and 46.7% with CLIP only to 56.3%.
method: Geometry reconstruction: SplaTAM-style 3DGS built from sparse RGB-D and odometry during frontier exploration, with a color/SSIM/depth loss.

Keyframe retrieval: after optimizing the current frame for p1=30 iterations, p2=60 iterations run on historical frames sampled with weights negatively correlated to PSNR, to reduce forgetting and surface holes.

Language injection: SAM instance masks and CLIP features are splatted onto Gaussians with intra-instance consistency and inter-instance separability losses (OpenGaussian-style). Features are quantized by a two-level codebook, coarse k1=32 on position plus language and fine k2=5 on language only, giving 160 entries. 2D-3D association ties each instance feature to a codebook entry.

Memory query: CLIP text or image embedding is matched by cosine similarity to codebook entries. The centroid of the matched Gaussians is projected onto the 2D obstacle map as a candidate waypoint, and FMM plans the path.

Goal verification: at 1.2 m from the waypoint the agent does a panoramic scan. Object and text goals pass if SEEM score >=1.1 or Mobile-CLIP similarity >=0.23. Image goals use LightGlue with inlier ratio >=5%. On failure the waypoint is marked invalid and the memory is re-queried.
Goalpoint navigation: the SEEM mask plus depth gives the object footprint on the obstacle map, the nearest traversable cell becomes the final goal, and the agent goes there and calls STOP.

GOAT-Core benchmark: 4 curated multi-room scenes, 24 episodes with 20 subtasks each (480 subtasks), with corrected text descriptions and single-floor tasks. It also supports goal localization evaluation.

setting.backbone: Modular pipeline of frozen models: SplaTAM-style 3DGS, SAM, CLIP/Mobile-CLIP, SEEM, LightGlue, FMM planner
setting.training_data: none for the models (frozen pretrained). Per-scene 3DGS and language features are optimized on that scene's exploration data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D plus odometry (640x480 RGB, HFOV 42°, depth 0.5-5 m)
setting.action_space: low-level MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, LOOK_UP/DOWN 30°, STOP, driven by FMM waypoint planning
setting.privileged: Pre-exploration of the full house by frontier exploration before the tasks. Baseline closed-set methods are given the target category list, LagMemo is not.

numbers_note: GOAT-Bench is not in the canonical list; it is mapped here to the closest listed name GOAT-Bench. Goal localization results are not given as SR/SPL: 70.8% average top-5 within 1.5 m on GOAT-Core (Object 88.4, Image 56.4, Text 66.8), against VLMaps 58.8%.
results: On GOAT-Core LagMemo reaches 56.3% SR and 35.3% SPL, beating the strongest baseline CoWs* (45.8% SR, 28.6% SPL) and Modular GOAT (38.3% SR). On the full GOAT-Bench it has the highest SR on Seen/Synonyms/Unseen (36.8/44.8/37.9), above Modular GOAT (26.3/33.8/24.9). Goal localization reaches 70.8% versus VLMaps 58.8%.
limitations: Localization depends on geometric fidelity, so sparse view coverage leaves blind spots. The memory is built offline after exploration (about 4200 s and about 500 MB per scene) and is not incremental or online.
The evaluation uses a curated 4-scene GOAT-Core, and the full-benchmark gains in SPL are smaller. It also assumes pre-exploration of the whole house.
Real-world results are qualitative only, with no quantitative numbers.
